solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Paper trail left after partnership formalised? (8)

annotation.definition: Paper trail left after partnership formalised?

blocks.note: reads as the documents a business deal leaves behind; the setter means real paper, scattered in a trail on the ground
reads as a firm's partners signing an agreement; the setter means a couple getting married

annotation.surface: An accountant's audit trail once a business partnership is signed off.
annotation.walkthrough: The business words — paper trail, partnership, formalised — point to an office; the partnership is a marriage, and the paper left behind is what guests throw at a wedding.
annotation.definitionFit: Confetti is the scattered paper left on the ground after a wedding.

entries.clue: Greek character drinking Sprite heading for architectural complex (6)

indicatorNotes.drinking: the Greek letter takes the sprite inside it, as a drinker takes in a drink
indicatorNotes.heading for: the head, or first letter, of the next word

blocks.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous sprite

annotation.surface: A Greek drinking a lemonade on the way to see some grand buildings.
annotation.walkthrough: Sprite reads as the soft drink the Greek is having, but it is a fairy; 'complex' is not a set of buildings but the psychological sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A complex in the psychological sense is an obsessive fear or fixation, which a phobia is.

entries.clue: Nancy’s really dated Republican? He’s unwelcome (10)

blocks.note: très is French for very; Nancy is a city in France

annotation.surface: Someone called Nancy has had a Republican boyfriend, and he is not welcome at home.
annotation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name, and 'dated' like going out with someone; Nancy is the French city, so her 'really' is in French.
annotation.definitionFit: A trespasser is someone on land where they are not welcome.

entries.clue: Lance quietly falling for female savage (6)

indicatorNotes.falling for: the P falls out and the F comes in for it

annotation.surface: A man called Lance quietly becomes infatuated with a wild woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Lance reads as a man's name and 'falling for' as falling in love; PIERCE swaps its P for F to give FIERCE.
annotation.definitionFit: Savage and fierce both describe violent, untamed behaviour.

entries.clue: Southerner endlessly jumping to this matter in formal document (8)

annotation.definition: to this matter in formal document

indicatorNotes.endlessly: both ends of the word are cut off
indicatorNotes.jumping: the letters leap about into a new order

blocks.note: SOUTHERNER without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A southern person keeps leaping up while filling in an official form.
annotation.walkthrough: Jumping looks like the Southerner's action in the scene; it is the instruction to rearrange what is left once both ends go.
annotation.definitionFit: Hereunto is legal language meaning 'to this' matter or document.

entries.clue: Caught opening carriage (4)

indicatorNotes.Caught: what you catch is what you hear

blocks.note: a gate is an opening in a fence

annotation.surface: Someone is trapped as they open the door of a carriage.
annotation.walkthrough: Carriage looks like a railway coach or horse-drawn vehicle; here it is the way you carry yourself when you walk.
annotation.definitionFit: Carriage is bearing or posture, and gait is the manner of walking.

entries.clue: Regret promoting English fur as ecofriendly (8)

indicatorNotes.promoting: the E is moved up a place, ahead of the U

blocks.note: to rue = to regret; RUE with its E (English) moved up a place

annotation.surface: Someone regrets advertising an English fur coat as green.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is that fur is the opposite of what campaigners call ecofriendly. In a down clue, promoting moves a letter higher up the column.
annotation.definitionFit: Something reusable avoids waste, so it counts as ecofriendly.

entries.clue: Aromatic spice in classy shiraz — wanting seconds! (6)

indicatorNotes.wanting seconds: the second, fourth, sixth… letters are missing

blocks.note: C l A s S y S h I r A z

annotation.surface: A wine note: a spicy aroma in a smart red, and the drinker wants a second glass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting seconds' sounds like asking for more wine; it means lacking the letters in even positions.
annotation.definitionFit: Cassia is a cinnamon-like bark used as a spice.

entries.clue: Harry: “I see worth differently” (9)

indicatorNotes.Harry: to harry is to harass, to push the letters about

annotation.surface: A quotation from Prince Harry about how he values things.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the speaker being quoted, but it is the verb telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in a different way.

entries.clue: Odd bits of airbed near field (5)

blocks.note: A i R b E d N e A r

annotation.surface: Scraps of an air mattress left lying close to a field after camping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits' looks like scraps of a torn airbed; it means the letters in positions one, three, five and so on.
annotation.definitionFit: Field in the figurative sense, a sphere of activity or contest, is the same image as an arena where contests are fought.

entries.clue: Kid’s book put back in bureau (3)

indicatorNotes.put back in: the B is moved to the back of the bureau

blocks.note: the FBI with its B taken out
standard abbreviation, placed at the back

annotation.surface: A child's book is returned to the writing desk.
annotation.walkthrough: The bureau is the FBI, the US Federal Bureau of Investigation, not a desk; moving its B to the end gives FIB. 'Kid' is the verb, to tease or fool.
annotation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tell them a small lie, to fib.

entries.clue: Diesel’s performance might be judged during such trials? (6,5)

annotation.definition: Diesel’s performance might be judged during such trials?

blocks.note: reads as how well a diesel engine runs; the setter means the acting of Vin Diesel, the film star

blocks.clueFragment: might be judged during such trials?
blocks.note: reads as engine testing on a rig; the setter means filmed auditions for a part

annotation.surface: An engine's diesel output being assessed in performance trials.
annotation.walkthrough: Diesel suggests a fuel or engine test; it is Vin Diesel, the actor, being auditioned on camera.
annotation.definitionFit: Screen tests are filmed auditions judging an actor's performance.

entries.clue: Critical view expressed by Spooner that’s often toasted? (7)

indicatorNotes.expressed by Spooner: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: key = critical, take = view (one's take on something); swap the first sounds

annotation.surface: A reviewer's harsh opinion that gets raised in a toast at dinners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Toasted' looks like drinks raised in honour; a teacake, a sweet fruited bun, is split and toasted.
annotation.definitionFit: A teacake is a currant bun usually eaten toasted.

entries.clue: Amphibian missing skin of pouch set free in the country (7)

indicatorNotes.skin of: the outer letters, P and H
indicatorNotes.set free: the remaining letters are let loose into a new order

blocks.note: its outer letters, removed to leave AMIBIAN

annotation.surface: A frog escapes from a bag and is released into the wild.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a frog let out of a bag; 'set free' is the instruction to rearrange AMIBIAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa.

entries.clue: Strategy mother has to house son held up by unfinished flat (6,4)

indicatorNotes.to house: mother takes the son inside her
indicatorNotes.held up by: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second

blocks.note: Latin for mother, a British public-school word
PLANE (a flat surface) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A mother must put her son up in a flat that hasn't been completed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has to' reads as an obligation; it just links mother to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a strategy is the overarching scheme that governs every smaller move, which is what a master plan names.

entries.clue: Time to split two rivers — American head making application (15)

indicatorNotes.to split: the T goes between the two rivers, splitting them

blocks.note: rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness country

annotation.surface: Time is running out to divide two rivers, and an American boss is applying for the job.
annotation.walkthrough: Head looks like a boss; it is a headland, NESS, common in Scottish place names. Application is not a form you fill in but hard work.
annotation.definitionFit: Application in the sense of hard, diligent work is industriousness.

entries.clue: Grotesque vice and depravity ultimately? (8)

indicatorNotes.Grotesque: the letters are twisted out of shape
indicatorNotes.ultimately: the last letter of the word before

annotation.surface: A moralist's summary of where grotesque vice finally leads.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: grotesque vice and depravity are what deviancy is.
annotation.definitionFit: Deviancy is departure from moral norms, the vice and depravity the clue lists.

entries.clue: Verbal attack — not the first, by the way (8)

blocks.note: a broadside is a fierce verbal attack; its first letter goes

annotation.surface: Someone launching into a tirade, adding 'by the way' that it isn't their first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By the way' reads as a throwaway aside, but it is the definition: beside the road.
annotation.definitionFit: Roadside means by the way, at the side of the road.

entries.clue: Feature in mounting Pirates, e.g. at Savoy? (5,3)

annotation.definition: Feature in mounting Pirates, e.g. at Savoy?

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the words that follow
indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards

blocks.note: piraTES EG AT Savoy, read backwards

annotation.surface: Something you would see in a staging of The Pirates of Penzance at the Savoy Theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the Savoy is the London theatre of Gilbert and Sullivan, whose Pirates of Penzance would be mounted there on a stage set.
annotation.definitionFit: A stage set is the scenery that features in any production.

entries.clue: Article on tax showing turnover for restaurant (7)

indicatorNotes.showing turnover: the whole string is turned over, back to front

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece about the tax on a business's takings, for a restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: Turnover looks like the business's sales figure; it is the instruction to reverse ANREVAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by general class: a taverna is the specific kind of small, informal restaurant found in Greece.

entries.clue: Canine perhaps mostly picking up smell as well (2,4)

blocks.note: a canine is a tooth; TOOTH without its last letter

annotation.surface: A dog seems to be sniffing out a scent as well.
annotation.walkthrough: Canine reads as a dog, and the smell as what it picks up; it is the pointed tooth.
annotation.definitionFit: To boot is an old phrase meaning as well, in addition.

entries.clue: Acerbic alternative rock (7)

indicatorNotes.alternative: an alternative arrangement of the letters

annotation.surface: A sharp-tongued review of an alternative rock band.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alternative rock' is a music genre; split it, and the rock is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Breccia is a rock made of angular fragments cemented together.

entries.clue: Baster ruined part of turkey (6)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked into a new order

annotation.surface: A cook's basting has spoiled the Christmas turkey.
annotation.walkthrough: A baster really is a turkey tool, so the surface reads naturally as a kitchen mishap; that is the camouflage for a straight six-letter anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: The breast is the prime carving joint of a turkey.

entries.clue: Vessels and sailors, it’s heard (6)

indicatorNotes.it’s heard: the sound of the words gives the answer

annotation.surface: Ships and their crews, according to rumour.
annotation.walkthrough: Vessels look like ships beside the sailors, but they are small table bottles, and 'it's' is part of the sound, not the grammar.
annotation.definitionFit: Cruets are small vessels for oil, vinegar or salt at table.

entries.clue: Stewed eel at pub? Yes, it’s good for the complexion! (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Stewed: the letters are cooked into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone recommending stewed eel from the pub as good for the skin.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's health claim for pub stew is absurd; the real skin tonic is a good night's sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: Beauty sleep is sleep said to keep you looking good.

entries.clue: Some keen retirees rearing bird (4)

indicatorNotes.Some: part of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.rearing: in a down clue, rearing up means reading upwards

annotation.surface: Enthusiastic pensioners raising birds as a hobby.
annotation.walkthrough: Rearing looks like raising chicks, which fits the bird; in a down clue it tells you to read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the tern, a slender, fork-tailed seabird, is one of crosswords' favourite short birds.

entries.clue: No pressure to throw up musical instrument (3)

indicatorNotes.No: 'No pressure' means without pressure, so the P that stands for pressure is left out of the word

annotation.surface: Advice that, if you are not under pressure, you won't be sick on a musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: Throw up looks like reversing or launching something; it is plain vomiting, PUKE, minus its P.
annotation.definitionFit: A uke is a ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar.

entries.clue: Happen to send a copy to our hosts (5)

indicatorNotes.hosts: OUR takes CC in as its guest

blocks.note: to cc someone is to send them a copy of an email

annotation.surface: Someone happens to copy in the people who are hosting them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Happen to send' reads as a single phrase; split it after Happen.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: events that happen are said to occur, and either verb works in 'accidents ___ at night'.

entries.clue: Take down tips for Newmarket in gloomy base (9)

indicatorNotes.tips for: the ends, here first and last, of the word
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the Newmarket tips inside the word for gloomy, as something sits in a box

blocks.note: its tips, first and last letters, inside DISMAL
e is the base of natural logarithms

annotation.surface: Someone noting down racing tips for Newmarket in a depressing army base.
annotation.walkthrough: Newmarket is the English horse-racing town, so 'tips' look like betting tips; they are its end letters. Base reads as a camp; it is the mathematical e.
annotation.definitionFit: Phrasal-verb synonym: taking down a tent or stage means pulling it apart piece by piece, as dismantling does.
